sections.heading: Document
sections.text:
COURSE DESIGN DOCUMENT
Further Education and Training Certificate: Information Technology – Systems Development
SAQA ID: 78965 | NQF Level 4 | 165 Credits

sections.heading: 1\. DOCUMENT CONTROL
sections.text:
Course Title | Systems Development Training Program for CET Lecturers
Qualification | FET Certificate: IT – Systems Development (SAQA ID: 78965)
Delivery Format | 15 Days / 75 Hours / 3 Blocks (Blended PBL Approach)
Target Audience | 20 TVET/CET Lecturers – Venda, Limpopo
Training Provider | Data Science Academy (DSA)
Primary Contractor | Muthwaks Solution
Client | CET College
Period of Service | Block 1: 02–06 March 2026 \ | Block 2: 23–27 March 2026 \ | Block 3: 13–17 April 2026
Daily Schedule | 09:00 – 14:00 (5 hours/day, 25 hours/block)

sections.heading: 2\. COURSE OVERVIEW & STRATEGIC ALIGNMENT
sections.text:
The primary goal of this training programme is to equip CET lecturers with practical systems development skills and ETQA-aligned assessment competence, enabling them to effectively supervise student projects and Work-Integrated Learning (WIL).
Element | Details
NQF Level | 4
Total Qualification Credits | 165
Credits Covered in This Module | 56 credits (via 10 prioritised unit standards)
Exit Level Outcomes Addressed | All 7: Communication, Systems Understanding, Problem-Solving, Programming, Teamwork, Task Execution, Technical Application
Critical Cross-Field Outcomes | Integrated throughout via PBL, local-language facilitation, reflective practice, and collaborative problem-solving
Pedagogy | Learner-centred \ | Project-Based Learning (PBL) \ | Agile-inspired sprints \ | Formative feedback loops \ | Contextualised to rural Limpopo
Language Strategy | English delivery with key concepts reinforced in Sepedi/Tshivenda; glossary provided
Tech Stack Focus | Python (logic/programming) \ | JavaScript/HTML/CSS (web scripting) \ | Git (version control) \ | Offline-first tooling for low-connectivity environments

sections.heading: 3\. SELECTED UNIT STANDARDS
sections.text:
Ten unit standards have been strategically selected to balance SAQA compliance, practical coding depth, and assessment feasibility within the 75-hour delivery window. The selection comprises 7 Core and 3 Elective standards, covering approximately 56 credits of the full 165-credit qualification.
ID | Unit Standard Title | Level | Credits | Component | Block | Assessment Method
1 | 14918 | Describe the principles of Computer Programming | 3 | 5 | Core (C) | 1 | Written reflection + code commentary
2 | 14910 | Apply the principles of Computer Programming | 4 | 8 | Core (C) | 2 | Live coding task + debug challenge
3 | 14915 | Design a computer program according to given specifications | 4 | 8 | Core (C) | 2 | Design doc + prototype demo
4 | 14927 | Apply problem solving strategies | 4 | 4 | Core (C) | 1 | Case study analysis + pseudocode
5 | 14924 | Demonstrate understanding of information systems analysis | 4 | 3 | Core (C) | 1 | Requirements workshop output
6 | 14933 | Demonstrate understanding of creating multimedia/web-based applications with scripting | 4 | 6 | Core (C) | 2 | Functional web form + JS validation
7 | 14920 | Participate in groups/teams to recommend solutions | 4 | 3 | Core (C) | 1 | Group presentation + peer feedback
8 | 14908 | Demonstrate understanding of testing IT systems against given specifications | 4 | 6 | Elective (E) | 3 | Test plan + bug report submission
9 | 14919 | Resolve computer user's problems | 4 | 5 | Elective (E) | 3 | Role-play scenario + support log
10 | 120379 | Work as a project team member | 4 | 8 | Elective (E) | 3 | Retrospective report + role reflection

sections.heading: 3.1 Component Breakdown Summary
sections.text:
Component | Count | Total Credits | Strategic Rationale
Core (C) | 7 standards | 41 credits | Mandatory technical backbone — non-negotiable for SAQA compliance and lecturer competency
Elective (E) | 3 standards | 19 credits | High-value practical skills (testing, support, teamwork) directly supporting WIL supervision and student mentorship
Fundamental (F) | 0 standards | 0 credits | Lecturers already possess NQF Level 3–4 communication/math competencies; focus retained on technical delivery skills

sections.heading: 3.2 Rationale for This Mix
sections.text:
• Compliance First: All 7 Core standards ensure the training meets the qualification's mandatory technical requirements.
• Practical Edge: The 3 Electives (testing, user support, project teamwork) directly support lecturers in supervising WIL and student assessments.
• Time-Efficient: Skipping Fundamental standards respects lecturers' existing NQF Level 3–4 competencies and keeps focus on new technical delivery skills.
• Flexible Scaling: If CET later wants a full 165-credit rollout, this 10-standard module serves as a perfect technical core foundation.
Recommendation: Maintain the 7 Core + 3 Elective mix. Fundamental standards (e.g., 119465, 9015) can be added later if CET explicitly requests coverage of communication or data literacy outcomes.

sections.heading: BLOCK 1: Foundations | 02–06 March 2026
sections.text:
Theme: "From Problem to Plan"
Day | Focus | Key Activities | Unit Standards | Deliverables
Day 1 | Welcome + Systems Thinking | Icebreaker, local tech challenges, SDLC intro, stakeholder mapping | 14924, 14920 | Stakeholder map + team charter
Day 2 | Programming Logic Fundamentals | Variables, conditionals, loops (Python), pseudocode practice | 14918, 14927 | Pseudocode exercises + logic flowcharts
Day 3 | Problem-Solving Frameworks | Decomposition exercises, flowcharts, debugging mindset | 14927, 14918 | Debugging checklist + case study solutions
Day 4 | Requirements & Design Thinking | User stories, use cases, wireframing a simple tool | 14924, 14915 | Requirements spec + low-fidelity wireframes
Day 5 | Team Sprint Kick-off | Form teams, define capstone scope, assign roles, Git basics | 14920, 120379 | Capstone project brief + Git repo initialised

sections.heading: BLOCK 2: Applied Programming & Design | 23–27 March 2026
sections.text:
Theme: "Build to Learn"
Day | Focus | Key Activities | Unit Standards | Deliverables
Day 6 | Functions & Modular Code | Writing reusable functions, error handling (Python) | 14910 | Modular Python script + error-handling demo
Day 7 | Web Scripting Basics | HTML forms, CSS styling, simple JS interactivity | 14933 | Functional web form with client-side validation
Day 8 | Program Design & Specs | Translating requirements to architecture diagram to code plan | 14915 | Design document + architecture sketch
Day 9 | Capstone Build Sprint 1 | Teams build prototype v1 (e.g., student feedback tracker) | 14910, 14915, 14933 | Prototype v1 + team progress log
Day 10 | Code Review & Iteration | Peer review, refactoring, intro to Git commits | 14910, 14920 | Reviewed code + Git commit history + reflection

sections.heading: BLOCK 3: Testing, Support & Assessment | 13–17 April 2026
sections.text:
Theme: "Quality, Reflection & Handover"
Day | Focus | Key Activities | Unit Standards | Deliverables
Day 11 | Testing Fundamentals | Writing test cases, manual vs. automated checks | 14908 | Test plan + executed test log
Day 12 | User Support & Troubleshooting | Role-play: handling lecturer/student tech issues | 14919 | Support scenario responses + troubleshooting guide
Day 13 | Capstone Build Sprint 2 | Finalise prototype, write user guide, prepare demo | 14908, 14919, 120379 | Prototype v2 + user guide (Sepedi/English)
Day 14 | PoE Compilation Workshop | Structure evidence, map to unit standards, self-assessment | All 10 | Draft Portfolio of Evidence (PoE)
Day 15 | Demo Day + ETQA Prep | Team presentations, feedback, moderation checklist, close-out | All 10 | Final PoE + presentation slides + moderation pack

sections.heading: Project Description
sections.text:
A simple, offline-capable web-based application that helps CET lecturers manage and track teaching activities:
• Log and track student project submissions
• Generate templated, customisable feedback
• Record and categorise common student technical issues
• Export basic reports for moderation and WIL documentation

sections.heading: Why This Capstone Works
sections.text:
Benefit | Explanation
Real-World Relevance | Directly addresses daily pain points for CET lecturers in Venda
Full Standards Coverage | All 10 unit standards are naturally embedded in the build process
Scalable Complexity | Teams can start with a basic HTML form and progress to validated, tested, documented solutions
PBL and Assessment Ready | Demonstrates teamwork, iterative development, and produces tangible evidence for ETQA moderation
Localisation Friendly | UI copy and support docs can be produced in Sepedi/Tshivenda + English

sections.heading: Team Deliverables
sections.text:
• Working Prototype: HTML/CSS/JS frontend + optional Python/Node backend (USB-deployable)
• Design Document: Requirements spec, wireframes, architecture diagram, data model
• Test Plan and Bug Log: Test cases, execution results, resolved issues
• User Support Guide: Troubleshooting FAQ + contact protocol (bilingual Sepedi/English)
• Portfolio of Evidence (PoE): Structured folder mapping all artefacts to the 10 unit standards

sections.heading: 6.1 Formative Assessment (During Learning)
sections.text:
Method | Purpose | Frequency
Daily Check-Ins | Gauge understanding, adjust pacing | Start/end of each session
Mini-Challenges | Reinforce concepts through quick application | 2–3 per day
Peer Code Reviews | Build collaborative critique skills | Days 10 and 13
Reflective Journals | Capture learning insights (local language optional) | End of each block

sections.heading: 6.2 Summative Assessment (For Credits / PoE Submission)
sections.text:
Component | Evidence Type | Mapped Unit Standards | ETQA Alignment Notes
Code Submission | GitHub repo export / USB backup with source code | 14910, 14915, 14933 | Version-controlled, commented, functional
Design Document | PDF with wireframes, specs, architecture | 14915, 14924 | Clear traceability from requirements to design
Test Plan | Checklist + executed test results + bug log | 14908 | Demonstrates systematic QA approach
Support Log | Scenario responses + troubleshooting documentation | 14919 | Shows user-centric problem resolution
Team Reflection | Retrospective report + role analysis + peer feedback | 14920, 120379 | Evidence of collaborative learning and growth
PoE Compilation | Structured folder with evidence index + self-assessment | All 10 | Moderation-ready: clear, organised, cross-referenced
Rubrics aligned to SAQA performance indicators and ETQA moderation requirements are provided for all components. All submissions are version-controlled and assessor checklists are included to ensure moderation-readiness.

sections.heading: 7\. LOGISTICS & RISK MITIGATION
sections.text:
Potential Challenge | Proactive Solution
Unstable Internet | Offline-first dev setup: VS Code + local Python/Node + pre-loaded USB resource packs; all materials downloadable pre-training
Varying Technical Levels | Tiered activities: 'Core' (mandatory for all) + 'Challenge' (extension for advanced); peer mentoring pairs
Language Accessibility | Key terms glossary in Sepedi/Tshivenda; facilitator trained in code-switching; bilingual support docs
Power Outages | Printed activity cards, whiteboard exercises, battery-backed devices; non-digital fallback activities pre-planned
Assessment Administrative Load | PoE templates + auto-checklists + digital submission guides to reduce marking burden on lecturers
Travel & Accommodation | Confirm early if R20k budget includes Venda logistics; if not, propose separate line item or DSA coverage

sections.heading: 8\. DELIVERABLES FROM DATA SCIENCE ACADEMY (DSA)
sections.text:
Pack | Contents | Format
Facilitator Pack | Slide decks, session plans, answer guides, local-language prompts, timing cues | PDF + PPTX + editable DOCX
Learner Pack | Participant guide, workplace logbook, PoE template, glossary (Sepedi/Tshivenda/English) | PDF + printable DOCX
Tech Pack | Offline dev environment setup guide, troubleshooting FAQ, USB image instructions | PDF + video tutorial + USB-ready folder
Assessment Pack | Rubrics per unit standard, moderation checklist, ETQA alignment matrix, assessor guide | PDF + Excel rubrics
Capstone Kit | Starter code, sample specs, demo video, evaluation rubric, team role cards | ZIP folder + printed quick-start guide

sections.heading: Immediate (Pre-Training)
sections.text:
• Confirm Budget Scope: Clarify with GT/Muthwaks if R20,000 includes travel and accommodation to Venda
• Finalise Unit Standard Sign-Off: Share this document with CET/Muthwaks for formal approval of the 10 standards
• Trainer Onboarding: Share Facilitator Pack and Tech Pack with assigned DSA trainer 2 weeks before Block 1
• Learner Pre-Work: Send a simple pre-training survey to lecturers (tech comfort level, language preference, expectations)

sections.heading: During Training
sections.text:
• Daily Feedback Loop: 5-minute end-of-day pulse check to adjust pacing and content
• PoE Progress Tracking: Use shared checklist to ensure evidence collection stays on track across all 3 blocks
• Local Context Integration: Encourage lecturers to adapt capstone examples to their own teaching subjects

sections.heading: Post-Training
sections.text:
• Moderation Support: DSA available for 2 weeks post-Block 3 to assist with ETQA submission queries
• Impact Report: Provide CET with a summary of learner outcomes, satisfaction scores, and recommendations for scale-up
• Pathway Guidance: Share articulation options for lecturers wishing to pursue the full 165-credit qualification

sections.heading: 10\. KEY QUESTIONS FOR STAKEHOLDER ALIGNMENT
sections.text:
The following questions should be confirmed with GT Thosago / Muthwaks Solution / CET College before Block 1 delivery:
• Is the R20,000 budget inclusive of trainer travel, accommodation, and per diems for Venda delivery, or are these costs budgeted separately?
• Will DSA issue certificates of completion, or is all assessment and moderation handled exclusively through CET's appointed ETQA?
• Are lecturers expected to continue mentoring student projects after the training? (If yes, Block 3 can include a WIL Supervision Toolkit module.)
• Does CET require Fundamental unit standards (e.g., communication, math) to be explicitly covered, or is the 7 Core + 3 Elective mix acceptable?
• Should the capstone project be standardised across all teams, or can teams propose their own lecturer-tool ideas within the agreed scope?

Project Description
A simple, offline-capable web-based application that helps CET lecturers manage and track teaching activities:
• Log and track student project submissions
• Generate templated, customisable feedback
• Record and categorise common student technical issues
• Export basic reports for moderation and WIL documentation

7\. LOGISTICS & RISK MITIGATION
Potential Challenge | Proactive Solution
Unstable Internet | Offline-first dev setup: VS Code + local Python/Node + pre-loaded USB resource packs; all materials downloadable pre-training
Varying Technical Levels | Tiered activities: 'Core' (mandatory for all) + 'Challenge' (extension for advanced); peer mentoring pairs
Language Accessibility | Key terms glossary in Sepedi/Tshivenda; facilitator trained in code-switching; bilingual support docs
Power Outages | Printed activity cards, whiteboard exercises, battery-backed devices; non-digital fallback activities pre-planned
Assessment Administrative Load | PoE templates + auto-checklists + digital submission guides to reduce marking burden on lecturers
Travel & Accommodation | Confirm early if R20k budget includes Venda logistics; if not, propose separate line item or DSA coverage
